Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> International BBC Three, BBC Scotland and Radio 4 Extra broadcast channels to close Source : BBC 20 October 2026 10:43pm Audio By Carbonatix
The BBC will close its BBC Three and BBC Scotland television channels in the spring, as the corporation continues to save £500m over two years.
Both services will become online-only, meaning they will continue to produce and host some content on iPlayer, without the need to fill a terrestrial TV schedule.
The BBC has also announced the closure of Radio 4 Extra, which largely airs speech programmes from the BBC's archive, including comedy, drama and documentaries.
BBC director-general Matt Brittin said: "We need to make every pound work harder for audiences as we respond to the immediate cost pressures and reinvent the BBC for a changing world. We all know that means tough choices."
Discussing the closure of linear broadcast services, Brittin said: "Much of the great content they currently carry will still be found where audiences already enjoy them on iPlayer and Sounds.
"While this follows media speculation, I recognise the confirmation of this news will be hard for audiences and colleagues."
BBC Three, aimed at young audiences and home to hits such as Fleabag, Normal People and Gavin & Stacey, moved online in 2016 but was reinstated as a TV channel in 2022.
BBC Scotland launched as a channel in 2019, broadcasting a variety of Scottish programming including news, sport, documentaries and entertainment.
However, some shows on the two networks, such as Two Doors Down on BBC Scotland and Sort Your Life Out on BBC Three, are repeats of episodes originally broadcast on other, more mainstream BBC channels.
Both networks currently broadcast TV programming only in the evenings, although BBC Scotland simulcasts BBC Radio Scotland for the rest of the day.
The BBC said that the network's nightly programme Reporting Scotland: News at Seven will not move to BBC iPlayer and will cease when the linear channel closes.
BBC Scotland's wider news offering will continue to serve audiences, including Reporting Scotland, The Sunday Show, Radio Scotland Breakfast, Debate Night and Scotcast, the corporation said.
While Radio 4 Extra airs some original programming, its schedule is mostly archive content, much of which is available on BBC Sounds.
Sir Peter Bazalgette, former chairman of ITV and production company Endemol, told BBC News: "This is a modest and pretty well-judged package.
"The essence of it is it protects the spending on content, it really cuts money in the distribution of programmes, and it really had to happen because the BBC has lost 30% of its revenue in 10 years."
But entertainment trade union Equity said Tuesday's announcement "does not signal a thriving BBC, and we are concerned about the UK's preeminent public service broadcaster's ability to meet its duties to the fullest".
Staff affected by the changes were told on Tuesday, although some media outlets had reported the proposed closure of BBC Scotland and BBC Three in recent weeks.
The BBC aims to cut between 1,800 and 2,000 jobs, almost one in 10, to save £500m over two years as it faces "significant financial pressures".
Around 550 job closures have already been announced in the news, while BBC Sport has so far announced more than 30 job cuts.
The newly appointed director of BBC News, Rachel Jupp, announced on Tuesday that the BBC is proposing a further £5.5m in savings, which would mean closing around 100 roles.
Meanwhile, the BBC has cancelled several high-profile TV series in recent weeks.The BBC has dropped
RuPaul's Drag Race UK, Blankety Blank, Celebrity Mastermind, Live at the Apollo, Football Focus, Ski Sunday, and Radio 4’s The World Tonight and You & Yours so far.
